part.text: The deep link brought up iOS’s “Open in Bluesky?” confirmation. I’m using a small XCTest UI runner to accept it and tap the in-app controls, then I’ll verify the Moderation screen.

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: project.yml
+name: SimControl
+options:
+  bundleIdPrefix: local.simcontrol
+  deploymentTarget:
+    iOS: "17.0"
+targets:
+  SimControl:
+    type: application
+    platform: iOS
+    sources:
+      - path: Host
+    settings:
+      PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: local.simcontrol.host
+      GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
+      SWIFT_VERSION: "5.0"
+  SimControlUITests:
+    type: bundle.ui-testing
+    platform: iOS
+    sources:
+      - path: UITests
+    dependencies:
+      - target: SimControl
+    settings:
+      PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: local.simcontrol.uitests
+      GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
+      SWIFT_VERSION: "5.0"
*** Add File: Host/Host.swift
+import SwiftUI
+
+@main
+struct HostApp: App {
+    var body: some Scene {
+        WindowGroup {
+            Text("UI test host")
+        }
+    }
+}
*** Add File: UITests/NavigationTests.swift
+import XCTest
+
+final class NavigationTests: XCTestCase {
+    func testOpenModeration() {
+        let springboard = XCUIApplication(bundleIdentifier: "com.apple.springboard")
+        let openButton = springboard.alerts.buttons["Open"]
+        if openButton.waitForExistence(timeout: 3) {
+            openButton.tap()
+        }
+
+        let bluesky = XCUIApplication(bundleIdentifier: "xyz.blueskyweb.app")
+        bluesky.activate()
+        bluesky.coordinate(
+            withNormalizedOffset: CGVector(dx: 0.075, dy: 0.095)
+        ).tap()
+
+        let settings = bluesky.buttons.matching(
+            NSPredicate(format: "label CONTAINS[c] 'settings'")
+        ).firstMatch
+        if settings.waitForExistence(timeout: 5) {
+            settings.tap()
+        }
+    }
+}
*** End Patch
